claim: Expert parallelism's per-GPU send volume in one all-to-all is approximately T*K*h*(EP-1)/EP (T local tokens, K top-k, h hidden dimension), and a full dispatch-plus-combine cycle doubles that volume.
stance_target: the repo's estimate that EP does two all-to-alls per MoE layer and that EP traffic scales with top-k and hidden size
scope_conditions: EP with local token count T, top-k K, hidden dim h, EP ranks
quoted_support: The per-GPU send volume in each all-to-all is approximately T*K*h*(EP-1)/EP, where T is the local token count, K the top-k, and h the hidden dimension; a full dispatch-and-combine cycle doubles this.

claim: Unoptimized all-to-all can consume up to 60% of total training time in MoE architectures like DeepSeek-V3 where experts span multiple nodes, because the sparse activation pattern provides limited computation to overlap with the communication.
stance_target: the repo's claim that EP is communication-bound on a slow fabric, and that the penalty is worse for MoE than for dense models
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V3-class MoE with experts spanning multiple nodes; unoptimized all-to-all
quoted_support: In architectures like DeepSeek-V3, where experts span multiple nodes, unoptimized all-to-all can consume up to 60% of total training time.

claim: Tensor parallelism applied to MoE experts is actively harmful: expert hidden dimensions are already small, so TP shards them into even smaller GEMMs while adding communication, which is why EP rather than TP is the natural MoE strategy.
stance_target: the repo's claim that tensor parallelism is ruled out for MoE work on this box — the argument holds even on NVLink hardware
scope_conditions: fine-grained MoE with small expert hidden dimensions
quoted_support: TP on MoE experts: Expert hidden dimensions are small; applying TP creates even smaller shards, reducing compute efficiency while increasing communication's share of total time.

claim: MoE training is fundamentally communication-bound unless parallelism is designed specifically for the parameter-compute asymmetry: per-token FLOPs scale only with active parameters while communication volume scales with top-k.
stance_target: the repo's claim that MoE experiments on this box must be designed around the fabric rather than around FLOPs
scope_conditions: MoE with K << E; any interconnect
quoted_support: The consequence: MoE training is fundamentally communication-bound unless parallelism is designed specifically for this asymmetry. This is not a matter of degree; it is a qualitative difference from dense models.

claim: DeepSeek-V3 has 685B total parameters but only 37B active per token, an 18x gap, which is why sharding expert matrices with tensor parallelism fragments already-small computations.
stance_target: the scale of the parameter-compute mismatch that makes EP necessary for large MoE
quoted_support: DeepSeek-V3 illustrates this concretely: 685B total parameters but only 37B active per token, an 18x gap.

claim: GEMMs account for about 70% of execution time in dense Llama-3 405B but under 50% in DeepSeek-V3, with token routing and permutation adding about 9% to layer execution time even after optimization.
stance_target: the claim that MoE training has a lower compute fraction and therefore less room to hide communication behind compute
scope_conditions: Llama-3 405B dense vs DeepSeek-V3 MoE; Megatron-Core measurements
quoted_support: In our measurements, GEMMs account for ~70% of execution time in Llama-3 405B (dense) but under 50% in DeepSeek-V3 (MoE)... Token routing and permutation, absent in dense models, add ~9% to layer execution time even after optimization.

claim: Megatron-Core offers three dispatcher backends — AllGather (simple but memory-intensive), all-to-all over NCCL, and Flex (DeepEP/HybridEP) — and the optimized Flex backends target NVLink-rich topologies like NVL72.
stance_target: the claim that the high-performance EP dispatchers presuppose NVLink, leaving only AllGather or plain NCCL all-to-all on a no-P2P PCIe box
quoted_support: The dispatcher then moves tokens to the GPUs hosting their assigned experts using one of three backends: AllGather (simple but memory-intensive), all-to-all (standard NCCL-based), or Flex (supporting optimized backends like DeepEP and HybridEP).

claim: Megatron-Core reaches 1,233/1,048 TFLOPS/GPU for DeepSeek-V3-685B and 974/919 TFLOPS/GPU for Qwen3-235B on GB300/GB200, roughly an order of magnitude above the ~162 TFLOPS/GPU the CMP 170HX box is claimed to deliver.
stance_target: the compute gap between a datacenter MoE training node and this box, as context for how much longer an MoE experiment will take
scope_conditions: NVIDIA GB300 and GB200 systems; DeepSeek-V3-685B and Qwen3-235B; FP8/NVFP4
quoted_support: On NVIDIA GB300 and GB200, it achieves 1,233/1,048 TFLOPS/GPU for DeepSeek-V3-685B and 974/919 TFLOPS/GPU for Qwen3-235B.

claim: MoE Parallel Folding decouples attention and MoE layer parallelism configurations, breaking the traditional EP <= DP constraint so attention layers can use TP=4 while MoE layers use ETP=1 with higher EP.
stance_target: whether a 5-GPU box can assign different parallelism to attention and MoE layers instead of one global topology
quoted_support: This separation enables Parallel Folding (Section 3.3): attention and MoE layers can use different TP/DP configurations. For example, attention layers might use TP=4 while MoE layers use ETP=1 with higher EP.
